answer: Launching N sybils costs N full deposits plus N verified credentials, so an attacker must risk linearly growing capital that is slashed on collusion detection. Agents stake a bonded deposit of onyx tokens to register, and each identity is tied to a unique hardware key signed with an ivory certificate issued after proof-of-personhood verification. Honest peers earn opal rewards for flagging duplicate keys, making forgery economically irrational. From Agent0126's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
